nodes.summary: The reduced form (Imbens & Angrist 1994): under independence, exclusion and monotonicity, with integrable potential outcomes and both arms of positive probability, the difference in mean outcomes between the arms is `𝔼[(Y(z, 1) - Y(z, 0)) 1_complier]`, for either `z`.
nodes.title: Reduced form: outcome difference is the complier-weighted effect

nodes.summary: The first stage (Imbens & Angrist 1994): under independence and monotonicity, with both arms of positive probability, the difference in treatment rates between the arms is the proportion of compliers.
nodes.title: First stage: treatment-rate difference equals complier share

nodes.summary: The mean of `f` in the arm `Z = z`, `𝔼[f | Z = z]`, the expectation under the conditional measure. It is the junk value `0` when `P(Z = z) = 0`.
nodes.title: Mean of a variable within an instrument arm

nodes.summary: The compliance type of the potential treatments `(D(0), D(1)) = (d₀, d₁)`.
nodes.title: Compliance type of a pair of potential treatments

nodes.summary: The four compliance types of Angrist, Imbens & Rubin (1996), determined by the pair of potential treatments `(D(0), D(1))`.
nodes.title: Compliance types of Angrist, Imbens and Rubin

nodes.summary: The compliers, `D(0) = 0` and `D(1) = 1`.
nodes.title: Compliers in a potential-outcomes model

nodes.summary: The Wald covariance identity when the instrument is independent of the residual.
nodes.title: Wald ratio identity for an instrument independent of the residual

nodes.summary: The Wald covariance identity: if `Cov(Z, U) = 0` and `Cov(Z, X) ≠ 0`, then `Cov(Z, Y) / Cov(Z, X) = β`. For a two-valued `Z` the ratio is the grouping estimator of Wald (1940), the difference of the group means of `Y` over that of `X`. This is a moment-condition identity, not a formal causal-identification result.
nodes.title: Wald ratio identity

nodes.summary: The Wald ratio as a ratio of regression slopes: the slope of `Y` on `Z` divided by the slope of `X` on `Z` (the form used with SNP–outcome and SNP–exposure associations) is `β`. This is again an observational moment identity.
nodes.title: Wald ratio as a ratio of regression slopes

nodes.summary: The ordinary least-squares coefficient identity for `Y` on `X` is `β + Cov(X, U) / Var(X)`, which differs from `β` exactly when `Cov(X, U) ≠ 0`.
nodes.title: Bias of the ordinary least-squares coefficient under confounding

nodes.summary: The covariance of any square-integrable variable with the outcome splits along the observational decomposition: `Cov(V, Y) = β Cov(V, X) + Cov(V, U)`.
nodes.title: Covariance with the outcome in a linear moment model

nodes.summary: The MR-Egger intercept under pleiotropy: it is the weighted mean pleiotropic effect `ᾱ_v` minus `Cov_v(γ, α) / Var_v(γ) · γ̄_v`.
nodes.title: MR-Egger intercept under pleiotropy

nodes.summary: The MR-Egger intercept `β̂̄_Y - slope · β̂̄_X` (weighted means).
nodes.title: MR-Egger intercept

nodes.summary: The finite-sample InSIDE identity (Bowden, Davey Smith & Burgess 2015): if the pleiotropic terms are uncorrelated with the instrument strengths in the weighted sense, `Cov_v(α, γ) = 0`, the MR-Egger slope is the coefficient `β` and the intercept is the weighted mean pleiotropic term `ᾱ_v`. This identity alone does not encode a causal interpretation.
nodes.title: InSIDE identity for MR-Egger

nodes.summary: The MR-Egger slope under pleiotropy (Bowden, Davey Smith & Burgess 2015): if the SNP–outcome associations are `Γ_j = α_j + β γ_j`, with pleiotropic terms `α_j` and SNP–exposure associations `γ_j`, the Egger slope of `Γ` on `γ` is `β + Cov_v(γ, α) / Var_v(γ)`.
nodes.title: MR-Egger slope under pleiotropy

nodes.summary: The MR-Egger slope (Bowden, Davey Smith & Burgess 2015): the slope of the weighted linear regression of `β̂_{Yj}` on `β̂_{Xj}` with an intercept, `Cov_v(β̂_X, β̂_Y) / Var_v(β̂_X)`. The paper's weights are `v_j = σ_j⁻²`.
nodes.title: MR-Egger slope

nodes.summary: The MR-Egger line is the weighted least-squares line: for nonnegative weights and `β̂_X` of nonzero weighted variance (so the total weight is positive and `β̂_X` is not constant on the support of the weights), it minimizes the weighted residual sum of squares.
nodes.title: MR-Egger line is the weighted least-squares line

nodes.summary: The weighted residual sum of squares `∑ v_j (β̂_{Yj} - a - b β̂_{Xj})²` of the line with intercept `a` and slope `b`.
nodes.title: Weighted residual sum of squares of a line

nodes.summary: Exclusion: the instrument affects the outcome only through the treatment, `Y(0, d) = Y(1, d)`.
nodes.title: Exclusion restriction for an instrument

nodes.summary: Independence (random assignment): the instrument is independent of the vector of all potential treatments and potential outcomes.
nodes.title: Independence assumption for an instrument

nodes.summary: Unbiasedness of IVW (Burgess, Butterworth & Thompson 2013), with the SNP–exposure associations `β̂_{Xj}` treated as fixed: if `β̂_{Yj} = β β̂_{Xj} + ε_j` with integrable mean-zero errors, the IVW estimator has mean `β`.
nodes.title: Unbiasedness of the IVW estimator

nodes.summary: The IVW estimator is the weighted mean of the ratio estimates with weights `w_j = β̂_{Xj}² / σ_j²`. This holds for all data: a SNP with `β̂_{Xj} = 0` has weight `0` and contributes nothing to either side.
nodes.title: IVW estimator as a weighted mean of ratio estimates

nodes.summary: The IVW estimator is the weighted least-squares slope through the origin: it minimizes the weighted residual sum of squares. This holds for all data: if every `β̂_{Xj} = 0` the sum does not depend on the slope (and `ivw` is the junk value `0`), and a SNP with `σ_j = 0` has weight `0` on both sides by Lean's `x / 0 = 0`.
nodes.title: IVW estimator minimizes the weighted residual sum of squares

nodes.summary: Directional pleiotropy biases IVW: if `Γ_j = α_j + β γ_j`, the IVW estimate is `β + ∑ γ_j α_j σ_j⁻² / ∑ γ_j² σ_j⁻²`. For example a common pleiotropic term `α_j = α ≠ 0` biases IVW whenever `∑ γ_j σ_j⁻² ≠ 0`, whereas a constant `α` satisfies InSIDE, so `eggerSlope_eq_of_inside` gives MR-Egger slope `β` and intercept `α`.
nodes.title: Directional pleiotropy biases the IVW estimator

nodes.summary: Without error, IVW recovers the proportionality coefficient: if `β̂_{Yj} = β β̂_{Xj}` for all `j` and some `β̂_{Xj} ≠ 0`, then the IVW estimate is `β`. This algebraic statement does not itself give `β` a causal interpretation.
nodes.title: IVW recovers an exact proportionality coefficient

nodes.summary: The first-order inverse-variance weight `w_j = β̂_{Xj}² / σ_j²` of the ratio estimate of SNP `j`, where `σ_j` is the standard error of `β̂_{Yj}` (Burgess, Butterworth & Thompson 2013).
nodes.title: Inverse-variance weight of a ratio estimate

nodes.summary: The inverse-variance-weighted (IVW) estimator `∑ β̂_{Xj} β̂_{Yj} σ_j⁻² / ∑ β̂_{Xj}² σ_j⁻²` (Burgess, Butterworth & Thompson 2013). The standard errors are positive in the model; it is the junk value `0` if every `β̂_{Xj} = 0`.
nodes.title: Inverse-variance-weighted estimator

nodes.summary: An observational linear moment model: variables `Z`, `X`, `Y` and `U` on a probability space, all square integrable, with the algebraic decomposition `Y = α + β X + U`. The residual `U` is an arbitrary observed-variable function. Consequently `outcome_eq` does not exclude direct effects of `Z` under interventions, and `β` is only the coefficient in this decomposition. Orthogonality (`Cov(Z, U) = 0`) and nonzero…
nodes.title: Linear moment model for instrumental variables

nodes.summary: A ratio with a Gaussian denominator has no first moment (a classical fact, recalled in the weak-instrument analysis of Burgess & Thompson 2011): if `D ~ N(m, v)` with `v > 0` and `N` is independent of `D` and not almost surely `0`, then `𝔼|N / D| = ∞`. Applied to the ratio estimator `β̂_Y / β̂_X` with a normally distributed SNP–exposure estimate `β̂_X`.
nodes.title: Ratio with a Gaussian denominator has infinite first moment

nodes.summary: Monotonicity: assignment never decreases the treatment, `D(0) ≤ D(1)`; there are no defiers.
nodes.title: Monotonicity assumption (no defiers)

nodes.summary: The ratio of two independent normal variables, the denominator with positive variance and the numerator not almost surely zero (`(mN, vN) ≠ (0, 0)`), is not integrable.
nodes.title: Ratio of independent normal variables is not integrable

nodes.summary: The observed outcome `Y = Y(Z, D(Z))`.
nodes.title: Observed outcome in a potential-outcomes model

nodes.summary: The observed treatment `D = D(Z)`.
nodes.title: Observed treatment in a potential-outcomes model

nodes.summary: A potential-outcomes model with a binary instrument and a binary treatment (Imbens & Angrist 1994; Angrist, Imbens & Rubin 1996): the assigned instrument `Z`, the potential treatments `D(z)` and the potential outcomes `Y(z, d)`, all measurable. The observed treatment is `D(Z)` and the observed outcome `Y(Z, D(Z))`. The identifying assumptions (independence, exclusion, monotonicity, relevance) are separate predicates.
nodes.title: Potential-outcomes model with binary instrument and treatment

nodes.summary: The ratio estimate `β̂_{Yj} / β̂_{Xj}` of SNP `j` (Lean's `x / 0 = 0` gives `0` when `β̂_{Xj} = 0`; such SNPs carry weight `0` in `ivwWeight`).
nodes.title: Ratio estimate of a single SNP

nodes.summary: The total weight is positive as soon as some SNP has `β̂_{Xj} ≠ 0`.
nodes.title: Positivity of the total IVW weight

nodes.summary: The observed treatment as a `0`/`1` real variable.
nodes.title: Observed treatment as a 0-1 real variable

nodes.summary: The compliance type of a unit.
nodes.title: Compliance type of a unit

nodes.summary: The first-order variance of IVW (Burgess, Butterworth & Thompson 2013): with the `β̂_{Xj}` fixed and `β̂_{Yj} = β β̂_{Xj} + ε_j`, where the errors are square integrable, pairwise uncorrelated (for instance independent) and `Var(ε_j) = σ_j²`, the IVW estimator has variance `(∑ w_j)⁻¹ = (∑ β̂_{Xj}² / σ_j²)⁻¹`.
nodes.title: Variance of the IVW estimator

nodes.summary: The unrestricted algebraic identity behind LATE. If the complier set has measure zero, both sides totalize to `0`; therefore this theorem is not an identification or complier-average claim at that boundary. Use `waldEstimand_eq_late` for the source-faithful result with relevance.
nodes.title: Unrestricted algebraic identity behind the LATE theorem

nodes.summary: The local average treatment effect theorem (Imbens & Angrist 1994, Theorem 1; Angrist, Imbens & Rubin 1996): under independence, exclusion, monotonicity and relevance, with integrable potential outcomes and both arms of positive probability, the Wald estimand is the average treatment effect among compliers, `𝔼[Y(1) - Y(0) | complier]` (read at either instrument value `z`, which exclusion makes irrelevant).…
nodes.title: Local average treatment effect theorem

nodes.summary: The Wald (instrumental-variable) estimand `(𝔼[Y | Z = 1] - 𝔼[Y | Z = 0]) / (𝔼[D | Z = 1] - 𝔼[D | Z = 0])`.
nodes.title: Wald instrumental-variable estimand

nodes.summary: The weighted covariance `∑ v_j (a_j - ā_v)(b_j - b̄_v) / ∑ v_j`, where `ā_v` and `b̄_v` are weighted means.
nodes.title: Weighted covariance

nodes.summary: The weighted mean `∑ v_j a_j / ∑ v_j`.
nodes.title: Weighted mean

nodes.summary: The weighted residual sum of squares `∑ (β̂_{Yj} - b β̂_{Xj})² / σ_j²` of the regression through the origin with slope `b`.
nodes.title: Weighted residual sum of squares through the origin

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
